Vanessa / team —

Thanks. From Legal's view: we should aim for a single overall liability cap in the MSA, but with a narrowly tailored data-incident "sublimit" concept in the Security Addendum that is functionally a carve-out for first-party remediation and customer notification costs. Key points:

1) Prefer sublimit at USD 1,500,000 (not 2M). That aligns better with our run-rate incident spend and keeps precedent reasonable.

2) Define the sublimit as applicable only where "Security Incident" meets the Security Addendum definition (unauthorized access/exfiltration confirmed by both parties after triage), with required incident response steps and evidence (forensic report, timeline). This prevents claim inflation.

3) We will not accept broad indemnification for regulatory fines. We can accept a narrow indemnity for third-party claims arising from our gross negligence or willful misconduct. For regulatory fines, we propose that those be subject to negotiation case-by-case and not automatically carved into the sublimit or outside the cap.

4) Consequential damages: maintain the standard mutual exclusion, but include explicit language that "remedial costs, notification costs, credit monitoring costs, and reasonable forensic investigation fees" are recoverable up to the sublimit.

5) Add a waterfall: (a) Redwood pays direct remediation & notification (b) SLA credits (if any) set off against damages (c) residual claims fall under the main cap. This gives commercial levers for escalation.

If Sales can accept 1.5M, I'll draft proposed redline language for both the MSA limitation section and Security Addendum linkage. Otherwise, I recommend escalating to Eric (VP Legal) for approval if ACME insists on 2M.

Rishi
General Counsel (acting) — Redwood Inference

Maya / Jordan —

Thanks for the redlines and the detailed ask. After internal review, Redwood can accept the concept of a narrowly-scoped data-incident sublimit, subject to the following position which I’m sending as a proposed compromise for ACME's team: 

1) Sublimit amount: USD 1,500,000 for "Security Incidents" as defined in the Security Addendum (see attached proposed language).
2) Scope of recoverable costs: limited to direct first-party remediation costs, notification costs, reasonable forensic investigation fees, and credit monitoring up to the sublimit.
3) Consequential damages remain excluded by mutual agreement. Regulatory fines remain outside the automatic sublimit and will be handled under indemnity only where Redwood is found to have been grossly negligent or to have engaged in willful misconduct; otherwise, regulatory penalties fall outside recovery absent express agreement.
4) Waterfall: remedial costs are paid first (within the sublimit), SLA credits (if applicable) may be applied as an offset, then any residual claim counts against the main MSA cap.

I’ve attached a clean redline that merges our proposed edits into your document (ACME_MSA_redlines_v2_merged.docx). If this is acceptable, please confirm and we will prepare the final paper for signature (DocuSign link below) and loop in Finance for countersign.
